intro: Learn common Spanish interrogative pronouns and adverbs: qué, quién, cómo, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, por qué, and cuál.
b1.texto:
In Spanish, question words carry a written accent mark in both direct and indirect questions: **qué**, **quién**, **cómo**, **dónde**, **cuándo**, **cuánto**, **cuál**, and **por qué**.

In questions with an explicit subject, the verb normally precedes the subject:
- *¿Dónde vive Ana?*
- *¿Cuándo es la clase?*

Note the difference between question and reason:
- **¿Por qué?** (two words, accented) asks why.
- **Porque** (one word, unaccented) means because in the explanation.
b5.f0.texto: Lucía asks curiously about her new classmate.
b5.f1.texto: She wants to know where he lives and when he studies.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo answers all her questions kindly.
b5.f3.texto: The student lives far away because he learns languages there.
b5.f4.texto: They write their phone number in the notebook.
b5.f5.texto: The two friends always chat with great enthusiasm.
b4.texto:
When asking questions with a question word and an explicit subject, the standard order is: question word + verb + subject.

We use **cuál** with the verb **ser** to ask for specific identity details, phone numbers, or addresses.
b6.pregunta: Which response properly answers «¿Por qué estudias español?»?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «porque» written as one word without accent explains the reason.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «por qué» with an accent mark is the question form.
b7.pregunta: Complete the question with the correct question word.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: use «cuál» with ser to request a specific piece of information.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: «qué es» asks for an essential definition.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «cómo» asks how or in what manner.
b8.traduccion: Why does he not live here?
p.qué.consejo: Interrogative pronoun used to ask about things, objects, or definitions.
p.quién.consejo: Interrogative pronoun for people. Plural form is quiénes.
p.cómo.consejo: Interrogative adverb asking about manner, condition, or state.
p.dónde.consejo: Interrogative adverb of place, written with an accent mark.
p.cuándo.consejo: Interrogative adverb of time, written with an accent mark.
p.cuánto.consejo: Interrogative of quantity matching gender and number: cuánta, cuántos, cuántas.
p.por qué.consejo: Two-word interrogative phrase with an accent mark asking for reasons.
p.cuál.consejo: Interrogative pronoun of choice or identity. Plural is cuáles.
p.porque.consejo: Causal connector written as one word without an accent mark to explain.
p.el número de teléfono.consejo: Masculine noun phrase referring to telephone contact details.
p.allí.consejo: Demonstrative adverb denoting a location away from both speaker and listener.
p.chico.consejo: Its feminine is «chica»; «ch» is one single sound, as in «chocolate».
p.número.consejo: The stress falls two syllables from the end, so «número» always carries a tilde on «ú».
p.teléfono.consejo: «teléfono» and «telefonear» share a root; the accent on «é» marks the stressed syllable.
p.curiosidad.consejo: The ending «-dad» turns an adjective into a noun: «curioso» becomes «curiosidad».
p.quiere.consejo: «qu» before «e» or «i» sounds like «k», and «ie» forms one stressed syllable.
p.responde.consejo: Its infinitive «responder» has the same strong, rolled «r» at the start of the word.
p.dudas.consejo: Its singular is «duda»; the «d» here is never pronounced like the English «th».
p.conversan.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b», so «conversan» is said «kon-BER-san», stressed on «ver».
p.entusiasmo.consejo: Words ending in «-asmo» are masculine, so it is «el entusiasmo», never «la».
